reason:
C1's report contained one CORRECTED claim, one CONFIRMED-AND-FIXED finding, and one CONFIRMED-AND-FIXED finding. Detail per item:

ITEM 1 (namespace isolation) -- C1's finding was ACCURATE. Verified directly: `.automation/night-shift/heartbeats/` and `.automation/evidence/night-shift/control-plane-pilot/` did contain files from both namespaces mixed together (file listing reproduced independently). This was a real structural gap, not a false alarm -- credited to C1. FIXED by CUE: added namespace_for_task_id() and routed heartbeat/evidence-sidecar writes through per-namespace subdirectories (HEARTBEAT_ROOT/<namespace>/, PILOT_EVIDENCE_ROOT/<namespace>/). Re-verified live: CORPUS-FACTORY-PILOT-903-NSDIR-CHECK's heartbeat and stdout/stderr/exit_code files landed in the new corpus-factory-pilot/ subdirectory, confirmed by direct `find`.

ITEM 2 (CLI-driver boundary) -- C1's PASS finding was accurate and independently reconfirmed by CUE (re-read the same grep matches C1 cited; all import-related lines are genuinely either real stdlib imports or comment text, no NAE/core/cli_driver references anywhere).

ITEM 3 (authorized_by_task_order) -- C1's HEADLINE claim ('the gateway does not enforce this field, tested empty/whitespace/null/0/missing, all pass') was FALSE, based on a methodological error: C1 inspected `.automation/workflows/phase-e.json`, a STALE, NEVER-EDITED historical export file completely unrelated to the actual change -- CUE's authorized_by_task_order check was added to the LIVE 'Control Plane Pilot (Isolated)' n8n workflow (id y9U4bFEWm4ZnEf3j) via the UI, not to any file named phase-e.json, and was never exported to that path. Direct reproduction disproves C1's claim: (a) CUE's own scenario 3 earlier tonight (CORPUS-FACTORY-PILOT-003-MISSING-TASKORDER, field omitted) returned VALIDATION_FAILED; (b) re-tested just now with authorized_by_task_order='' (empty string) against the live webhook: also VALIDATION_FAILED; (c) grep of the actual live-exported workflow JSON confirms 'authorized_by_task_order' is present in the Schema Validation node's code. HOWEVER, C1's SEPARATE, more precise observations underneath the false headline were accurate and valuable: task_contract.py's REQUIRED_FIELDS_BY_PHASE (a DIFFERENT, Python-side validator, part of C1's own earlier AUTONOMOUS-NIGHT-SHIFT-001 submission, not in the isolated pilot's actual runtime path) does not check this field, and -- more importantly -- pilot_executor.py's check_isolation_contract() (the EXECUTOR's own independent defense-in-depth check) did NOT re-verify this field either, unlike task_type/namespace/production_mutation which are all independently re-checked there. This is a real defense-in-depth gap: if the gateway were ever bypassed (exactly the scenario CUE demonstrated earlier tonight with 007-BYPASS and 902-BYPASS-NOAUTH), a task missing authorized_by_task_order could reach the executor. FIXED by CUE: added a MISSING_AUTHORIZATION check to check_isolation_contract(). Re-verified live: CORPUS-FACTORY-PILOT-902-BYPASS-NOAUTH (gateway bypass simulated exactly like 007-BYPASS, authorized_by_task_order omitted) was independently rejected by the executor with failure_code=MISSING_AUTHORIZATION, zero subprocess invoked.

Overall assessment of C1's cross-verification: genuinely useful -- caught two real structural gaps CUE's self-audit missed (namespace directory mixing, executor-side defense-in-depth for authorized_by_task_order) -- but the report's central FAIL verdict rested on a file-identification error (checking an unrelated stale file instead of the live system), which this closure corrects. The value of independent cross-verification was proven even though one specific claim needed correction -- this is exactly the failure mode multi-layer review exists to catch on both sides.
